title: Second-opinion technical review for city data center deals
one_liner: A fixed-fee package for small cities facing a data center: adversarial review of the developer's noise, water and power submissions, plus a term sheet built from the few community benefit agreements that exist.
customer: Planning directors, city managers and county administrators in jurisdictions under a data center moratorium or first inquiry, mostly populations of 5k-150k that cannot afford a big-firm consultant. They pay $8k-25k per package, and the cost can often be recovered from the applicant through an escrow for third-party review.
problem: Small governments are negotiating blind against developers' consultants. Broken Arrow, OK issued an RFQ for consultants to 'advise on environmental, water, noise, utilities and fiscal modeling' and needs recommendations by year-end 2026 or a moratorium extension. Fort Worth voted unanimously for a moratorium, Chicago introduced one in September 2026, and Lexington, KY paused approvals until at least Oct 31, 2026. NPR reports that deals such as the one in Boyce, Louisiana were negotiated under NDAs. The Federation of American Scientists found only eight executed community benefit agreements, only one fully executed and publicly posted (Lancaster, PA), and says 'best practices are not readily available'.
solution: A productized package. (1) An ordinance with fill-in standards: setbacks, dBA limits at the property line, closed-loop or reclaimed-water requirements, decommissioning bond, and utility-capacity verification. (2) A fiscal calculator comparing abatement to service and infrastructure costs, plus water/wastewater and power-interconnection checks. (3) A term-sheet library annotated from the known executed CBAs. (4) A retained on-call review of the developer's noise study, water plan and load forecast by contract engineers, with a plain-language memo the council can read in open session. Moratorium end dates are natural deadlines that pull purchases forward.
why_now: Data center siting became the top local land-use fight of 2026: Wixom MI, Denver, Fort Worth, San Antonio, Lexington, Broken Arrow and Chicago all acted this year, and more cities keep opening moratorium clocks. Developer NDAs are now a political issue, which pushes officials to buy independent review.
revenue_model: $8k-25k fixed fee per package; $2.5k/month retainer during active negotiation; per-review fee for developer-funded escrow; a subscription comparables database (abatement terms, water allocations, decommissioning bonds) for state municipal leagues.
non_obvious_insight: Ordinance templates are free and cities can copy them; the scarce thing is an adversarial reader of the developer's technical submissions, because the city's only counterpart is the developer's own consultants under NDA. Applicant-funded escrow lets the city avoid a budget fight, so procurement is quick. Evidence: Broken Arrow's RFQ scope and year-end deadline (https://citizenportal.ai/articles/9481196/oklahoma/tulsa-county/broken-arrow/city-council-meetings/city-forms-datacenter-study-committee-says-ordinance-moratorium-remains-in-place); the gap in best practices and only eight executed CBAs (https://fas.org/publication/data-center-community-benefit-agreements/); NDA-shrouded deals (https://www.npr.org/2026/08/27/nx-s1-5879528/data-center-nda-disclosure-louisiana); Fort Worth's unanimous moratorium (https://fortworthreport.org/2026/08/12/data-center-moratorium-takes-first-steps-after-fort-worth-city-councils-unanimous-vote/).
first_30_days: Publish a free comparison of the eight known CBAs and a one-page 'questions to ask a data center developer' for planning directors. Email 30 planning directors in cities with moratoria expiring in the next 6 months. Line up 2 retired utility or acoustic engineers as contract reviewers. Sell 2 fixed-fee review memos at $6k each, ideally funded by the applicant's escrow.

title: DKIM for Bank Accounts: Signed Payee Records
one_liner: A free, domain-verified payment record that suppliers publish, plus an AP plug-in that blocks any bank-detail change the supplier's own domain has not signed.
customer: Bookkeeping and accounting firms, and AP teams at 20-500 person companies on QuickBooks, Xero, Bill.com or NetSuite. Suppliers publish for free.
problem: BEC cost $3.05B in 2025, about 3.4x the $893M IC3 tags as AI-related, yet the money and attention go to deepfake detection. Bank-detail change requests still arrive by email or phone and get 'verified' by calling a number supplied in the same message. Small firms have no fraud team, and 3 seconds of audio now clones the voice they trust.
solution: A supplier proves domain control (DNS TXT plus a signed JSON file: legal name, hashed account and routing numbers, valid-from and valid-to dates, rotation contacts). A browser extension and accounting-app add-on compares any vendor bank details at bill entry and payment approval against that record. It hard-warns on mismatch and routes changes through a supplier-initiated, delayed, out-of-band confirmation flow. Every check is logged as evidence for the firm's crime-insurance social-engineering endorsement.
why_now: Cloned voices and AI-written invoices have broken the callback-and-voice-check control. IC3's 2025 numbers show BEC is still the largest business loss pool. Instant rails like FedNow and RTP make wrong payments irrevocable. Accounting platforms now have open app stores that allow a third-party control at the moment of payment.
revenue_model: $5-9 per client company per month for accounting firms, or $19-29 per AP seat for in-house teams. Suppliers are free. Later, per-check API fees from payment platforms and insurer-funded discounts.
non_obvious_insight: BEC is a provenance problem for one string of digits, not a media-authenticity problem. Email fraud fell when SPF/DKIM anchored trust in domain ownership, and the same move works for payee data. Selling through accountants avoids the two-sided cold start: each supplier who publishes instantly protects every customer of theirs that uses a participating firm.
first_30_days: Publish an open spec, a Chrome extension and a read-only Xero/QuickBooks add-on. Recruit 10-15 bookkeeping firms (30-100 clients each) through ProAdvisor and bookkeeper communities. For each firm, send its 20 largest vendors a five-minute publish flow. Convert 10 firms to $99/month plans.

title: Book the Unbookable: Agents for Offline Suppliers
one_liner: A voice-and-WhatsApp agent phones, negotiates and confirms bookings with small inns, guides and boat operators that have no API, then turns each one into bookable inventory.
customer: Independent travel advisors and small DMCs first, later AI trip-planning apps and OTAs seeking long-tail inventory.
problem: The best small inns, agriturismi, ryokan, guides and boat operators take bookings by phone, WhatsApp or email in local languages, with deposits by bank transfer. Advisors spend hours per booking, AI agents cannot book them and OTAs do not list them. Hotel-side voice AI is crowded (for example Dextr AI's seed), but buyer-side is empty.
solution: A real-time multilingual voice and text agent calls or messages the supplier, checks availability, negotiates a net rate within the advisor's limits and sends the deposit. A human verifies the money step. Every completed booking builds a structured supplier profile (hours, languages, deposit rules) that becomes API-bookable next time.
why_now: Real-time voice models now handle 30+ languages, WhatsApp Business is universal, and agentic payment tooling exists. Shrinking booking lead times and rerouted travel create demand for fast alternatives beyond OTA inventory.
revenue_model: USD 20-60 or 3-5% of booking value per booking from advisors, SaaS for DMCs, and later a take rate from suppliers and inventory data licensing.
non_obvious_insight: Long-tail supply is invisible to agents because it lacks an API, not because it lacks quality. The cheapest API is a phone call made by a machine with a human closing the money step, and each call builds an inventory graph nobody owns.
first_30_days: Pick Japan, Italy and Greece. Recruit 15 independent travel advisors and process 100 bookings semi-manually with human voice operators shadowing the agent at USD 30 per booking. Measure time saved and conversion.

title: Consented Elder-Speech Data Co-op via Storytelling Clubs
one_liner: Senior-living oral-history clubs where residents opt in, get a life-story book and pay, and their de-identified speech is licensed under strict speech-recognition-only, no-cloning terms to voice-AI and ambient-scribe companies.
customer: Speech-AI, ambient clinical documentation, hearing-aid and companion-robot teams buying elder-speech training and test data (per audio hour). Senior-living operators host the clubs for engagement and a revenue share, and families receive the recordings.
problem: Voice and scribe AI is tuned on younger speech and underperforms on 80+ voices, hearing-aid users and dementia, Parkinson's or stroke speech. AI labs now need clean chain-of-title (Suno swapped to a licensed-data model on Sep 9), and older adults are adopting AI (23% of 65+) while distrusting how their data is used (69% of 50+ are uncomfortable sharing health records with AI). The people who could supply ethical data, and who deserve to be paid for it, have no rights infrastructure.
solution: Trained facilitators (retired teachers, social workers) run recorded storytelling sessions in senior-living communities. Every participant passes a capacity screen with a family or health-care-proxy co-signature and can withdraw. Each clip carries a machine-readable consent scope (recognition and understanding only, never voice synthesis or cloning), is de-identified, and is tracked in a rights ledger that supports revocation and audit. Residents receive cash, the community gets a share, and families get an edited memoir and audio archive.
why_now: Licensed-data pressure is peaking after music and text lawsuits, and the EU AI Act Art. 50 transparency rules began applying in Aug 2026. Voice AI is being pushed on seniors just as they adopt it, and the 80+ cohort is the fastest growing group in the country.
revenue_model: Buyers pay roughly $80-150 per audio hour under a per-dataset license. About 25-30% goes to participants, 15% to the host community, and the rest covers facilitators and platform costs. Family memoir and archive packages are a $149-299 upsell.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce thing is not more hours of speech. It is consented hours from the oldest speakers, and only eldercare operators can gather them ethically, because capacity screening, proxies and revocation are the whole product. The strictest license terms (recognition only, no cloning) are what let elders and families say yes.
first_30_days: Pilot in 3 communities with an ethics review from a local university IRB or elder-law adviser. Record about 40 hours and secure a letter of intent from 2 to 3 elder-focused voice or scribe teams for a 100-hour dataset. Use the memoir book as the participant-facing hook.

title: Wearable-Verified PE Credit for ESA Families
one_liner: Turn any kid's fitness tracker into an audit-proof PE transcript line and an ESA service receipt.
customer: Homeschool and microschool families, co-ops and umbrella schools (about $10-15 per student per month). ESA administrators and clearinghouses (compliance contracts). Gyms and studios that want to bill ESA funds.
problem: PE is the least-supported homeschool subject. ESA homeschoolers get a fraction of what private-school kids do (about $2,000 versus $10,474 in Texas) and must spend in a closed vendor marketplace. ESA programs are audit-anxious. Local climbing gyms, swim schools and martial-arts studios cannot clear vendor onboarding. Screen-fatigued parents want real movement documented.
solution: An app plus a $40-60 band, or existing Garmin/Apple/Polar data shared with parent consent. It logs moderate-to-vigorous minutes and coach-attested skill milestones. It converts them into Carnegie-unit PE credit on a transcript issued through a partner accredited umbrella school. It also generates tamper-evident 'service delivered' receipts for ESA reimbursement. A vendor-of-record wrapper handles W-9, insurance and background-check attestations so a local gym can bill ESA funds. Parents control the data and only summaries leave the family account.
why_now: With 31 states opted into the 2027 federal scholarship credit and ESAs expanding, auditors and SGOs will demand evidence that services were actually delivered. Homeschool ESA marketplaces are closed and clunky. Alpha School has normalized heart-rate monitoring of kids, consumer wearables are ubiquitous, and 61% of teachers want less screen time.
revenue_model: $12 per student per month from families or co-ops. $2-5 per verified session or receipt from ESA clearinghouses. A 5-8% vendor-of-record fee on gym and studio ESA billings.
non_obvious_insight: As tens of billions of public scholarship dollars start to flow, the winning tools will be the ones that produce evidence of delivered service as a byproduct. A heart-rate trace is a hard-to-fake delivery receipt, and PE is the one subject where wearables give clean proof. Fitness providers' idle daytime hours are the supply, and education compliance is the demand.
first_30_days: In one ESA state (AZ or FL), recruit 8-10 homeschool co-ops and 3-5 climbing, martial-arts or swim studios. Sign an accredited umbrella school to issue the PE credit. Enroll about 100 kids for a semester at $12 a month. Ship a minimal web app that ingests Garmin/Apple Health exports plus coach attestation. Take the pilot data to one ESA clearinghouse.

title: One Recert: Housing Paperwork Keeps Medicaid Coverage
one_liner: Reuse the income and employment paperwork affordable-housing operators already collect every year to stop residents' Medicaid from lapsing under the new work requirements, paid per retained member by Medicaid health plans.
customer: Medicaid managed-care organizations in expansion states (pay per retained member-month or per completed redetermination), plus LIHTC/HUD affordable-housing owners (pay per unit for lower delinquency and turnover). Hospitals in expansion states are a third payer.
problem: Work requirements hit all 41 expansion states on Jan 1, 2027 (Nebraska has been live since May 1, 2026), with 5.5-6.3M projected coverage losses and a 12.5-14.2% operating-margin hit to hospitals. Losses are mostly paperwork failures rather than true ineligibility (Arkansas's 2018 experiment saw about 18,000 people drop off largely through reporting failures). Each lost member is lost capitation for the plan, unpaid bills for the hospital and, later, a late-rent risk for the landlord.
solution: With resident consent, ingest the annual and interim income/employment verifications that housing operators already gather. Map them to state rules (80 hours a month, or roughly $580 in monthly income, plus exemptions such as caregivers), build the compliance packet, submit it to the state portal or plan, and send monthly nudges when hours dip. A remote call team plus the property's resident-services coordinator handles the human steps.
why_now: The Jan 1, 2027 nationwide deadline is three months away and plans are setting 2027 retention budgets now. Nebraska is a live proving ground today. ACA subsidy expiry already added about 4.8M uninsured, so plans and hospitals are hunting for any lever that keeps members covered.
revenue_model: Per-member-per-month retention fee or $75-150 per completed redetermination from plans; $2-4/unit/month SaaS from housing owners; hospital-funded pilots.
non_obvious_insight: Affordable-housing recertification is the most audit-grade employment and income record low-income adults have, and nobody reuses it. The housing operator is also the only party that sees the resident monthly and has its own reason to care, since Medicaid loss leads to medical debt and then late rent.
first_30_days: Start in Nebraska. Sign one affordable operator with 1,000-3,000 units and one Medicaid plan. Hand-build the packet workflow with forms and spreadsheets for 100 consenting residents, measure retention against a comparison group, and price the service per retained member. Clone state by state ahead of Jan 1.

title: The True Acceptance Map for Rural Transfers
one_liner: Voice AI agents call every receiving psychiatric unit and specialty hospital each night to learn what they will actually accept, and rural ERs text a number to find out who will say yes.
customer: Critical access hospital EDs, state hospital associations and state rural health offices (paid with Rural Health Transformation Program funds), and state behavioral health authorities. Subscription per hospital or per state.
problem: A rural ER holding a suicidal 16-year-old, or a stroke, trauma or OB patient, may spend 3-8 hours making phone calls to place them. State bed registries say beds are open, but the real decision is made by a house supervisor at 2am applying unwritten rules: no IV drug history, no one-to-one sitter, no autism, no patients over 250 lb, no out-of-state Medicaid, no aggression, and no calls after 9pm without a physician-to-physician call. Every ER charge nurse keeps a battered binder or a phone note of who says yes to what and who to ask for. It lives in one head, and it goes out of date when a house supervisor changes.
solution: Use voice agents to call each facility's intake line on a schedule and extract structured, current answers: true open capacity by population, unwritten exclusions, insurance rules, the name and direct number of the person who decides, and the hours that person answers. Serve it back through a plain SMS interface. A nurse texts 'psych, 16yo, Medicaid, sitter needed, hx cutting' and gets a ranked call list with the exact script to use (the words that get an acceptance). Only facility rules are collected. No patient data is ever in the calls. Later, sell a receiving-side listing so facilities can pre-qualify referrals and get fewer dead-end calls.
why_now: Every state has now posted Rural Health Transformation Program funding opportunities (as of August 2026), and care coordination and access technology are core uses. Research on bed-tracking systems shows registries still leave clinicians phoning to check appropriateness, especially for aggressive, medically complex, autistic and dementia patients. Voice agents from 2025-26 can now hold a natural two-minute call with an intake nurse for a few cents. The workforce shortage means intake lines are answered by fewer people, which makes the tacit rules more valuable.
revenue_model: $300-600 per ER per month for SMS access. State-level licenses of $100-300k per year paid from RHTP or behavioral health funds. A second line is a receiving-facility listing at about $500 per month per facility. The proprietary asset is a data graph of real rules that no registry has.
non_obvious_insight: The valuable data is not bed counts, which are wrong within an hour. It is the tacit acceptance criteria and the identity of the human who decides, and it can only be learned by phone at night. That is why bed-registry vendors (built on hospital self-reporting) miss it. Facilities that discover their rules are being published accurately will cooperate, because a dead-end call costs them time too.
first_30_days: Pick one state or region. Type up the founder nurse's own binder, about 60-80 facilities, into a spreadsheet. Wire an off-the-shelf voice agent platform to call each facility nightly and write results to a table. Put an SMS bot in front of it with a Twilio number. Give it free to five ERs in the region and compare call counts and time to placement before and after. Bring the numbers to the state hospital association and the RHTP office.

title: Ex-Sales-Rep Route Collectives for Critical-Metal Scrap
one_liner: Commission-only teams of laid-off SDRs and inside-sales reps that each own a territory and sign machine shops and dental and electronics labs to take-back programs for tungsten carbide and cobalt scrap. Lots are aggregated and sold directly to domestic reclaimers.
customer: Sellers: tens of thousands of small generators such as machine and tool-and-die shops, carbide grinding shops and dental labs. Buyers: domestic carbide and tungsten reclaimers and refiners that now need US-allocated feedstock. Reps: displaced sales staff.
problem: The BIS rule restricts tungsten scrap exports and the DoD and DOE are subsidizing domestic supply, but supply is scattered across small generators who sell to local yards at a steep discount or trash the hard-to-value streams such as grinding swarf. The bottleneck is sales coverage of the long tail, not recovery technology. Entry-level SDR and BDR roles are among the first white-collar jobs AI is absorbing, leaving a large pool of trained cold-outreach talent.
solution: Each rep owns a metro territory and signs 30-100 shops to a free take-back program: lockable bins, an assay or XRF-based price sheet, payment by lot and simple compliance paperwork (including BIS and toll-processing documentation). Consolidate through partner yards or carriers and sell aggregated lots to reclaimers on term offtake. Start with carbide inserts and grinding swarf, then add cobalt-alloy turnings. Reps keep 15-25% of the net spread and a software backbone handles pricing, pickup scheduling and payouts.
why_now: The BIS allocation rule created a domestic-first buyer set. Machine shops are squeezed by tariffs and input costs and welcome found cash. SDR and entry-level sales roles are being cut in 2026 and reps are actively looking for commission work. The DOE ($134M) and DoD rare-earth and critical-mineral funding raise buyers' willingness to pay for documented domestic feed.
revenue_model: Spread on aggregated lots (buy at a fixed percentage of the reclaimer price and sell at the offtake price). Service fee on compliance paperwork. Later, SaaS for yards and reclaimers.
non_obvious_insight: In critical-material recycling the scarce resource is neither collection technology nor recovery chemistry but sales coverage of thousands of tiny generators. The people best at long-tail coverage are exactly the ones AI has just made cheap.
first_30_days: Pick one machine-shop-dense metro. Get a reclaimer to sign an offtake letter. Recruit five ex-SDRs and have them call 500 shops from public industrial directories. Collect and sell the first few tons of carbide and swarf, and document real price gaps versus the shops' current yards.

title: Size Ladder: Circular Wardrobes for GLP-1 Users
one_liner: A subscription that ships the next clothing size on the GLP-1 titration schedule, takes back the last, stores a 'restart' wardrobe, and routes the excess into resale and recycling, sold through telehealth partners as a retention perk.
customer: Cash-pay GLP-1 patients ($59-129 a month), telehealth and clinic operators paying a per-member fee for retention, and plus-size apparel brands and textile-EPR schemes that need diverted volume.
problem: Users move through three to five sizes in 12-18 months, and only about a third are still on therapy at one year while roughly 60% of ex-users plan to restart and stoppers regain about two thirds within a year. So closets fill with clothes that fit neither the current body nor the likely future one. The US textile recycling rate is 14.7% and California alone landfills 1.2M tons a year. Telehealth players have converged on the same $149-$349 price, so they need non-price loyalty features.
solution: At each dose step or every 10 lb, ship the next size from a pooled inventory of pre-owned and new pieces, take back the previous size, and offer take-in tailoring as an alternative. A 'restart wardrobe' bank holds the prior size for 12 months for a small fee. With consent, the telehealth partner shares titration stage so the platform can forecast sizes; in return the clinician sees a behavioral signal when size changes stall or reverse.
why_now: Cash-pay pills at $149 have widened the user base (22% of households have a user) and moved buying away from insurers to consumers who are already spending more on skincare and fragrance. California's textile EPR (SB 707) is moving toward fee-setting, creating a funded outlet for take-back volume. Compounding's exit has pushed users onto branded cash-pay channels that want stickiness.
revenue_model: Consumer subscription, partner PMPM fees ($3-6) from telehealth for retention, brand sponsorship from apparel companies, and resale margin plus EPR diversion credits on the outflow.
non_obvious_insight: Titration is a clock. Because dose steps predict weight-loss milestones, the apparel demand curve is forecastable in a way no fashion category ever is, and the closet is the earliest behavioral read-out of regain.
first_30_days: Recruit 50 patients from GLP-1 patient communities and one partner clinic. Source pre-owned plus-size inventory cheaply from thrift and textile sorters. Line up a tailor network. Run a 3-month pilot at $79 a month, tracking return rates, size churn and how well titration stage predicts the next size.

title: Consumer-Side Debt Negotiation Agent for Brazil
one_liner: A WhatsApp agent that reads a household's Open Finance data and negotiates all its debts on the debtor's behalf.
customer: Over-indebted Brazilian households, paying a success fee.
problem: Household debt is around 82% by the cited indicator, delinquency is at a record, and Lula's Sep 25 relief may reach under 1% of defaults. People face many creditors and rarely know discounts are available.
solution: With consent, pull debts from Open Finance, build a repayment plan, negotiate through lender collection channels and debt portals, and set up Pix Automatico debits. The wedge is revolving card debt and overdraft for low-income users.
why_now: Open Finance and Pix Automatico are mature and LLM agents can now negotiate reliably. The online betting ban leaves ex-bettors with debts and no plan.
revenue_model: 10-15% of the discount obtained, charged only on success.
non_obvious_insight: Existing collections platforms are lender-paid and optimise recovery. A debtor-side agent exposes rate arbitrage and gives lenders a rational counterparty at scale.
first_30_days: Run a concierge pilot with 100 users, using humans plus AI drafting, to learn discount rates by lender. Check consumer-protection rules first.

title: AI-Native Estate Settlement Firm Under Arizona ABS
one_liner: A licensed alternative business structure that runs uncontested probate and small-estate work end-to-end at a flat fee, with attorneys supervising agent-driven workflows.
customer: Families of decedents in Arizona with $100K-$2M estates (uncontested probates, small-estate affidavits, simple trust administration), referred by funeral homes, hospices, senior living communities and advisors.
problem: Hourly or percentage probate fees don't work for $300K estates, so many attorneys decline them. Families face 9-18 months (unverified estimate) and $5-20K bills, run by an overwhelmed executor.
solution: An Arizona ABS-licensed law firm using agent workflows for documents, court filings, creditor notices, asset inventory, accountings and distributions, with attorney supervision at ratios far above traditional practice. Fixed price ($2,900-$6,500) with a timeline guarantee, payable from the estate at closing, and one point of contact. Add-ons include real estate sale and tax return preparation.
why_now: Arizona has permitted non-lawyer ownership of law firms since 2021 and Utah runs a sandbox. LLMs are now reliable enough for supervised legal drafting, and Arizona has a large retiree population. The brief's estimate of $5T of yearly transfers is heavily weighted to the very wealthy, leaving middle-class estates unserved.
revenue_model: Flat fees plus ancillary margin on property sales, tax preparation and accounting.
non_obvious_insight: Hourly legal billing can't profitably serve middle-class estates, but a licensed software-first structure can undercut on price while earning better margins. The regulatory sandbox is both wedge and moat.
first_30_days: Apply for the ABS license or white-label under an existing ABS. Sign 3 funeral homes or senior communities for referrals. Run the first cases with a supervising attorney, and get counsel to review unauthorized-practice and fee-sharing rules.

title: Special-Tool Exchange for Retiring Regional Fleets
one_liner: Buy or take on consignment the OEM special tooling stranded when regionals retire 50-seat jets and older turboprops, calibrate it, and rent or sell it to operators who cannot get it from the OEM for months.
customer: MROs and Part 145 shops adding a regional-jet or turboprop type, Part 135 and cargo operators, freighter-conversion programs, and operators in Latin America, Africa and Asia flying older regional types. Sellers are regional airlines and lessors with tooling cages to empty.
problem: Every type needs OEM special tooling: rigging pins, wing and gear jack adapters, engine sling adapters, pinning tools, pressure-test rigs, borescope adapters, prop and control-rigging fixtures. New from the OEM this is expensive and lead times can run to months, and some tooling is out of production. When a regional retires a subfleet, that tooling is on the tool-control ledger at near-zero book value, taking up cage space. It gets scrapped, shipped out with airframes, or forgotten. Buyers who are desperate for it have no idea the seller exists, and vice versa.
solution: A consignment marketplace and rental pool. Take tooling in from retiring fleets at no cash outlay, on a 70/30 split of sales and rentals. Inspect it, get it recalibrated through a metrology lab, tag it with a certificate, and catalog it with photos and drawing references. Rent it weekly or monthly with a deposit and freight, or sell it. Offer starter tooling bundles for a shop taking on a new type, such as everything needed for a first C-check on that airframe.
why_now: Majors keep replacing 50-seat regional jets and older turboprops with larger regional aircraft, so tooling cages empty every quarter. Cargo conversions and second-life operators in emerging markets are keeping the old types flying. OEM lead times and parts availability have been poor across the industry since 2022, so buyers will pay to skip the wait.
revenue_model: Consignment split on sales, rental fees at roughly 3-6% of replacement value per month, calibration and freight margin, and bundle pricing for new-type start-ups. Later, a subscription for shops that want guaranteed access to a tooling pool.
non_obvious_insight: Tooling has none of the obsolescence problem of parts. It does not expire except for calibration. A directors of maintenance would rather give it away than pay to store it, and nobody knows who the buyers are. The unusual thing about this business is that the inventory is almost free and the demand is urgent, because a missing pin can ground an airplane for weeks.
first_30_days: Call 20 directors of maintenance, tech-services managers and lessor technical reps whose subfleets are winding down. Get two or three tool cages on consignment with no upfront cash. Photograph and catalog them, send calibrated items to a local metrology lab, and publish a simple catalog with rental terms and a deposit process. Contact freighter-conversion programs, Part 135 operators and international MROs that fly the same type. The first rental should close within weeks, because the urgency price is high.

title: Under-Canopy Grave Detection Survey Service
one_liner: Find unmarked graves before the bulldozer does, using drone LiDAR that sees through trees, machine-learning triage and targeted ground-penetrating radar.
customer: Municipalities, state DOTs, developers, title companies, utilities and solar or pipeline builders, plus churches and heritage nonprofits.
problem: Lost and unrecorded burial grounds are usually discovered when earthmovers hit them, causing delay, cost and heartbreak. Historic cemeteries, especially those of marginalized communities, are often undocumented. GPR surveys are slow, costly per acre and limited by scarce operators. There is no burial-risk layer in due diligence.
solution: Drone LiDAR and photogrammetry across large tracts to detect depressions and anomalies under canopy, ML-ranked into a probability map, followed by targeted GPR verification of the top candidates. Deliver a survey report and a registry entry. Add LLM reading of handwritten cemetery and church records.
why_now: Survey-grade drone LiDAR is now cheap, ML for GPR and terrain anomalies has matured, and rural land is being cleared quickly for solar, data centers and pipelines. LLMs can now read handwritten historic records. Everstory's drone mapping of about 400 cemeteries shows the method works for known sites.
revenue_model: $200-$1,500 per acre depending on terrain and depth, annual subscriptions for DOTs and utilities, and data licensing to title insurers.
non_obvious_insight: Every earthmoving project carries burial-risk liability that appears in no database. The same survey serves developers, heritage groups and families, so it can be financed by the party with the most to lose.
first_30_days: Pilot with 2 churches or heritage groups on grant-funded work. Rent a LiDAR drone and pitch 5 solar developers on due-diligence add-ons. Recruit a GPR contractor and a cultural-resources archaeologist for sign-off.

title: Year-Round Books for Immigrant-Community Tax Storefronts
one_liner: Give community tax preparers WhatsApp-native, in-language AI bookkeeping so they can serve their small-business clients all year.
customer: Independent tax storefronts in Latino, Vietnamese, Korean, Chinese and other immigrant communities, each serving 100-500 micro-business clients (taquerias, nail salons, owner-operator truckers, cleaners, roofing crews) who show up with a shoebox once a year.
problem: The clients have no monthly books. Preparers can't do year-round bookkeeping without adding headcount, and they cannot afford Intuit's or H&R Block's offering. Silicon Valley assumes better AI will close the trust gap, but these owners trust a person who speaks their language.
solution: White-label intake through WhatsApp, WeChat or KakaoTalk: the client sends receipt photos and voice notes in their language, and AI drafts the ledger and a monthly P&L. The preparer reviews exceptions in a queue and sends a plain-language summary. Sales tax, payroll deposits and quarterly estimated tax reminders are included. All output carries the preparer's brand.
why_now: Multilingual and code-switched voice transcription became reliable in 2025-26. IRS Direct File ended for 2026, and Intuit cut 17% of staff while opening about 600 offices and 20 TurboTax storefronts, which suggests trust stays human and local.
revenue_model: $99/month per storefront plus $12 per client per month, or a 30% revenue share on a $150 per client monthly bookkeeping fee.
non_obvious_insight: The trust problem is already solved by a human who is embedded in the community. What the preparer lacks is leverage, and the incumbents are hiring storefronts, not selling to them. AI turns a seasonal tax business into a year-round one.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 storefronts in one metro through ITIN and tax-prep associations and Spanish-language radio. Pilot with five clients each on WhatsApp Business. Charge nothing until the storefronts see retention and added revenue, then set the per-client price.

title: Business Identity Watch: LifeLock for LLCs
one_liner: Continuous monitoring of the state filings, liens and listings that define a small business, with a fast response kit when someone hijacks them.
customer: Owners of LLCs and sole proprietorships, reached through community banks, insurance agents, CPAs and registered-agent companies.
problem: Formation is cheap and online, and US domestic companies no longer file beneficial-ownership reports (FinCEN's final rule, August 2026). Census restated its formation series and excluded internet-sales-linked applications from some series, which suggests formation counts are polluted by non-real businesses (inference). Fraudsters can file fake officer or agent changes, register lookalike LLCs and domains, hijack listings and file bogus liens. Owners find out when a collections letter arrives.
solution: Monitor Secretary of State filings across states with open bulk feeds, UCC indexes, lookalike entity names and domains, and Google Business Profile edits. Alert the owner and provide pre-drafted correction filings, fraud affidavits, a registered-agent switch, and a bank notification letter.
why_now: There is no federal ownership registry to lean on, formation is cheap, and AI makes synthetic-identity and lookalike-business fraud cheaper to run.
revenue_model: $9-19 per entity per month, a $299 incident-response fee, and bulk banking deals at about $2 per entity per month.
non_obvious_insight: The state filing is the root of trust for a small business, and nobody watches it. Identity-theft companies watch people, not entities, and a bank that already knows the business is the natural distributor.
first_30_days: Pick five states with open bulk filing data and build change alerts. Pilot with 200 LLCs through one community bank or bookkeeper. Track fraud events detected and time to resolve.

title: Permit-as-Firmware Groundwater Pump Governor
one_liner: A smart pump controller that hard-enforces a farmer's groundwater allocation and lets an agent trade unused acre-feet with neighbors before the pump ever exceeds its limit.
customer: Irrigated growers (almonds, pistachios, alfalfa, wine grapes) in California's regulated groundwater basins, especially San Joaquin Valley subbasins with adopted allocations and overpumping penalties. Groundwater sustainability agencies (GSAs) are the channel and co-payer.
problem: Allocations are enforced after the fact from meter reads. Kings County's agency, for example, set a $500-per-acre-foot charge for pumping above base allocation, with penalties slated after the 2026 water year. Probationary subbasins (Tule, Tulare Lake) add $300-per-well registration and a $20-per-acre-foot state fee. Farmers overshoot by accident, water trades run through brokers and phone calls, and GSAs cannot verify compliance without costly audits.
solution: A retrofit device on the well's starter or VFD, tied to a certified flow-meter reader, keeping a live allocation ledger. It soft-throttles as the budget nears zero, and can hard-stop with a paid override that 'borrows' at the penalty price. The grower's dashboard or agent can pre-bid to buy or sell units on a subbasin exchange. The GSA receives a read-only, tamper-evident compliance feed and can give fee discounts for participating wells.
why_now: Allocation-based enforcement begins in earnest with the 2027 water year, and the state has already put two San Joaquin Valley subbasins on probation. Water prices and fallowing pressure make trading valuable. Cellular and LoRa IoT and smart motor starters are now cheap.
revenue_model: $1.5-3k per well install, $50-150 per month per well, a 1-2% fee on water trades, and GSA grants or fee credits that subsidise compliance metering.
non_obvious_insight: The law is already a constraint. The product turns a legal budget into a physical budget, like a hard credit limit on a card. Growers want the stop because it converts unpredictable $500-per-acre-foot penalties into a controllable budget, and GSAs want it because self-reporting becomes verified data. Sell it as insurance against fines, not as smart irrigation.
first_30_days: Pick one subbasin with adopted allocations and penalties. Recruit 3 pump-service companies as install partners, since they own the relationship with the well. Pilot free on 5 wells in exchange for testimonials and data. Ask the GSA general manager for a compliance-metering pilot grant.

title: Contingency Recovery of Missed Rotable Repair Warranties
one_liner: A success-fee auditor that finds repaired aircraft components that failed inside the shop's warranty window, and turns them into filed claims and cash.
customer: Small and mid-size operators with their own stores and a thin materials team. That means regional airlines, Part 135 cargo feeders and air-ambulance fleets, and Part 145 shops that buy their own exchange units. They pay 20-25% of whatever cash or credit is recovered, and nothing up front.
problem: A repaired starter-generator, bleed valve, hydraulic pump or fuel control that fails 4 months after the shop visit is often covered by warranty. Almost nobody claims it. The tech pulling the unit at 3 AM is trying to make a 6 AM departure and never sees the warranty terms. The repair invoice sits in accounts payable as a PDF. The removal record sits in the maintenance system, and hours and cycles sit in a third place. One materials coordinator owns thousands of removals a year, with 30-90 day claim windows. Three other leaks go unclaimed as well: 'no fault found' evaluation fees on units that were still under warranty, unreturned exchange cores that turn into penalty charges, and repair turnaround-time guarantees that shops never credit because nobody compares PO date to receipt date.
solution: Ingest three exports: removals and installs, PO and repair invoices (PDFs read with an LLM extractor), and the negotiated warranty terms. Match by part number and serial number, including interchangeable P/Ns. Flag every in-warranty failure, late repair turn, disputable NFF fee and open core. Then draft the claim on each vendor's own template, track it to a paid credit, and re-run monthly. Add a 3 AM 'is this unit under warranty?' lookup for maintenance control, so the claim gets started at the moment of removal.
why_now: Airline cost pressure on regionals is high, and mechanic wages rose sharply in 2024-2026, so labor cost per removal is up. Materials teams are being cut while fleets stay old. LLM invoice and PDF extraction only became reliable and cheap enough in the last 18 months, and that is the missing link, because the money sits in unstructured AP documents that MRO software never reads.
revenue_model: Contingency fee of 20-25% of recovered cash and credits, with a 12-month tail on the audit. Later add a $2-5k per month SaaS tier for continuous monitoring, and sell benchmark data on shop warranty behavior to airline procurement teams.
non_obvious_insight: The leak is not in the maintenance system, it is in accounts payable. The tech who removes the part, the coordinator who could file the claim and the department that paid the invoice never share a screen. MRO software vendors will not fix it because warranty terms live in negotiated PDFs, not fields. Repair shops know most eligible claims are never filed, and they price that into their rates. A contingency auditor is the same playbook as freight-audit and telecom-audit firms, aimed at a niche nobody has covered.
first_30_days: Pitch 10 directors of maintenance and materials managers at small regionals, cargo feeders and helicopter EMS operators. Offer a free 12-month leakage audit, and ask them for the three exports. Build the matcher in Python plus an LLM invoice parser, and use a retired warranty or materials coordinator as a paid advisor for vendor quirks. Deliver a ranked claim list to the first 2-3 customers, file the claims yourself, and sign the success-fee agreement on the first credit memo. Publish the aggregate audit finding, such as the percentage of eligible failures that were never claimed, as the lead magnet.

title: Model-Swap Regression Service for Contractors
one_liner: Automated testing and porting that lets defense contractors re-platform their AI workflows to a different model vendor in weeks without losing quality.
customer: Defense integrators, primes' AI teams and mid-size government contractors whose workflows were tuned around one model family and must now change vendors.
problem: The D.C. Circuit upheld the DoD supply-chain-risk designation of one model vendor on Sept 26, and DoD is moving classified workloads off it by October. Contractors are cutting that vendor's use. Their prompts, agents and evaluation sets were tuned for one model, and nobody can prove a replacement performs equally on their real tasks.
solution: Capture the contractor's existing workflow traces, build a task-specific eval set, run it across Gemini, ChatGPT, Grok and open-weight models, and auto-rewrite prompts and tool schemas to reach parity. Deliver a signed parity report usable as evidence for the government customer.
why_now: The designation is a fresh legal fact with an October deadline. Vendor politics now shape the supply chain, and lawful-use terms differ by vendor. Model swapping is now a compliance event, not an engineering preference.
revenue_model: $40-200K per migration project, then $3-10K per month for continuous cross-vendor regression monitoring.
non_obvious_insight: The designation is not a one-time event. Every future vendor dispute will force the same migration, so the durable product is a standing eval-and-port harness for a politically volatile model market.
first_30_days: Post a fixed-price migration audit at $15K. Contact 15 small integrators and GenAI.mil agent builders through defense AI communities. Reuse one eval harness across clients while keeping each client's data separate.

title: Fifteen-Minute Court Reporting for Family Law Hearings
one_liner: Remove the half-day minimum by dispatching remote stenographers into many short hearings per day, so a family-law litigant gets a certified record of a 15-minute hearing for about $100.
customer: California family law and probate attorneys and solo practitioners. Self-represented litigants reached through DV legal aid organizations and family law facilitators. Legal aid groups buying bulk credits. Later, county courts contracting to meet the new duty to provide records to indigent litigants.
problem: California logged roughly 3 million civil, family and probate hearings without a verbatim record between April 2023 and March 2026, about 7 in 10. Without a record, appeals of custody and restraining-order rulings fail, because the appellant cannot show error. Private reporters charge $250-$500+ appearance minimums, since a reporter can wait 2-3 hours for a 12-minute calendar item. Nobody pays that for a routine hearing. In 2026 the California Supreme Court (Family Violence Appellate Project v. Superior Court) held that courts must give indigent litigants an official verbatim record on request, and courts do not have the reporters to comply.
solution: A dispatch platform that reads court calendars, predicts when each matter will be called from historical hearing-type durations per department, and pages a remote reporter into the court's Zoom or Teams feed only for the minutes needed. One reporter covers 8-12 short hearings a day across departments. Deliver a certified transcript in 24-72 hours, with an AI first draft for the reporter to scope. Price is a flat $95 for hearings up to 15 minutes and about $8 per page beyond that. Start where remote appearance and remote reporting are allowed (California's AB 3013 authorizes remote reporting, and each court's procedures need checking). Pitch courts on per-department-day capacity at a discount to staffing a full-time reporter.
why_now: The 2026 California Supreme Court ruling creates a legal duty courts cannot currently meet. AB 3013 (2024) opened remote reporting. The workforce is projected to be about 5,500 reporters short by 2030. Family courts are widely on video. Reporter dead time is a scheduling problem that software can solve.
revenue_model: Per-hearing fees paid by attorneys and litigants. Bulk credits funded by legal aid and foundation grants. Later B2G contracts priced per courtroom-day. The reporter keeps about 55-60% of each hearing fee, which beats their typical hourly yield because dead time is eliminated.
non_obvious_insight: The reporter shortage is partly a utilization problem. In a busy family calendar department, a reporter may write 2-3 hours of a 7-hour day and wait the rest. Remote hopping sells that dead time to several litigants at once, so the price can fall 70% while the reporter earns more.
first_30_days: Sign 3-5 remote-capable freelance or semi-retired reporters. Pick one county whose family departments run on Zoom and cover it manually with a shared spreadsheet and a text pager. Offer 10 solo family law attorneys and two DV appellate nonprofits (start with the Family Violence Appellate Project) at-cost coverage of their next 5 hearings. Track wait time per hearing so the prediction model has real data.

title: Verification Service for Satellite Imagery Authenticity
one_liner: Check whether a satellite image is real, and issue a chain-of-custody certificate for images used as evidence.
customer: Trade-finance banks and collateral managers, property and cargo insurers, sanctions and compliance teams, and newsroom verification desks.
problem: Generative AI can now fake satellite images, and fakes circulated during conflicts in 2025 (prior knowledge). Imagery is increasingly used as evidence for loans against stockpiles, insurance claims, sanctions cases and environmental claims. Fraud incentives rise with that value, and nobody certifies pixels.
solution: A verification API that checks a submitted image against multi-provider archives (free Sentinel and Landsat plus commercial partners) and physical consistency (sun angle, shadows, sensor geometry). Partners can sign images at ingestion with a provenance manifest. Deliver certified 'as-of' extracts for legal use.
why_now: Generative image quality crossed the threshold in 2025-26. Imagery archives are large and multi-source, and providers are looking for premium 'verified' tiers. The briefing notes decision products for regulated buyers remain open.
revenue_model: $20-200 per verification. Enterprise subscriptions of $30-150k per year. Revenue share with imagery providers on verified tiers.
non_obvious_insight: Detection models age quickly, but archive access does not. The moat is a cross-provider archive and provenance partnerships, not a classifier.
first_30_days: Assemble a test set of real and synthetic images. Build a reverse-lookup against Sentinel-2 and Landsat. Run free verifications for two commodity-finance firms and one newsroom, then convert one to a paid annual license.

title: Shared Certified Operators for Tiny Water Systems
one_liner: A marketplace pairing retired and semi-retired certified water operators with mobile-home parks, small towns and rural systems that must legally have one and cannot hire one.
customer: Mobile-home parks, towns under 3,300 people, rural water districts, and schools, campgrounds and churches on their own wells. They pay $600 to $2,500 a month per system. Supply side: retired plant operators, and operators laid off by consolidations.
problem: Regulations require a state-certified operator in responsible charge. Roughly 30% to 50% of the workforce is retiring within a decade, small systems cannot offer a full-time salary, and losing the operator means violations, fines and boil notices. New lead and PFAS monitoring adds workload.
solution: Vet and license-match operators state by state, pair each with a cluster of 8 to 12 nearby systems, and run telemetry-based oversight (cheap chlorine-residual, tank-level and pump-current sensors) so the certified person supervises remotely while a local non-certified lead hand does routine tasks. The platform handles state contract-operator paperwork, liability insurance, scheduling and compliance reporting.
why_now: Retirements are hitting small systems hardest. Cheap LTE-M and satellite-capable water sensors make remote supervision affordable. Public SDWIS violation data provides a ready-made, ranked lead list.
revenue_model: Monthly retainer per system with the platform keeping 25% to 35%. Sensor kit resale or lease at about $1,500. Insurance and compliance-reporting add-ons. Later: state programs paying to reduce violations.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce input is not labor hours; it is the legal signature of a certified operator. One operator with telemetry can responsibly oversee ten tiny systems, and the regulator's own violations database is the sales list.
first_30_days: Pull SDWIS operator-certification and monitoring violations for one state. Recruit 3 retired operators via the state operator association. Sign 3 to 5 mobile-home parks at about $750 a month with compliant contract-operator letters and install a $1.5k telemetry kit.

title: Placement Proof for Workforce Pell Providers
one_liner: A verified job-placement and completion ledger that makes short-term training programs (CDL, CNA, welding, HVAC, medical assistant, cosmetology) audit-ready for the governor and Secretary approvals that Workforce Pell requires.
customer: Small proprietary career schools, community college workforce and continuing-education units, and employer-training nonprofits running 8-15 week programs. The program owner or director pays. State workforce boards are a second buyer because they were given no new resources to verify placement.
problem: The Workforce Pell final rule (published May 19, 2026; effective July 20, 2026, with early implementation from July 1) covers programs of 150-599 clock hours and 8-15 weeks. A program must show 70% completion and 70% job placement, measured over the 12 months before it applies and annually after that. The governor must first certify the program as high-skill, high-wage or in-demand, then the Secretary approves. Providers must submit completer lists and the information needed to verify placement. Commenters flagged burden for small providers and noted states got no new resources to run the framework. Separately, the earnings-premium rule (effective July 1, 2027) strips Direct Loan access from programs that fail in two of three consecutive years. The Department estimated 93% of cosmetology programs would fail under the proposal.
solution: At completion the system automatically sends completers and employers text and email verification requests at 30, 90 and 180 days. It collects pay stubs, employer confirmations and consent for state wage-record matching, and reconciles them to the rule's placement definition. It produces the governor's application packet (completer list, placement evidence, tuition versus earnings benchmarks) and the annual recertification. It also scores each existing program's exposure to the earnings-premium test using public program-level earnings data so owners can decide what to keep, fix or convert into a short-term program.
why_now: The 12-month look-back means a provider that is not tracking verified placement now cannot apply in 2027. The earnings-premium test takes effect July 1, 2027 and is already being scored on 2021 completers' 2025 earnings. States are building governor-approval processes this fall, and Workforce Pell went live July 2026.
revenue_model: $4-12k per year per program subscription, or $150-300 per completer verified. $3-5k fixed fee for the governor application packet. Earnings-premium exposure report for $1.5-3k. Later, licensing to state workforce boards for verification.
non_obvious_insight: The binding constraint is not program design but evidence: 70% verified placement with a 12-month clock that starts before the application. Short-course providers such as CDL, CNA and barbering schools typically track completion, not verified employment, so most will discover the gap after the clock has started. The final rule requires providers to give the Governor 'necessary information to verify the job placement rate', and it aggregates small programs' completers up to four award years to reach a 30-student minimum, which favors providers with clean historical records. The Title IV survival angle (93% of cosmetology programs were projected to fail the earnings test under the proposal) gives the same customer a second, more urgent reason to buy. Sources: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/19/2026-10013/accountability-in-higher-education-and-access-through-demand-driven-workforce-pell-pell-grant and https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/01/2026-13286/accountability-in-higher-education-and-access-through-demand--driven-workforce-pell-student-tuition
first_30_days: Pick two states whose governors have opened a Workforce Pell approval process. Recruit five schools in different fields, including one at-risk cosmetology school, with a $1.5k pilot price. Backfill the last 12 months of completers by text and employer email to produce a baseline verified placement rate. Deliver a sample governor packet and an earnings-premium exposure score for each. Use the results to pitch the state workforce board on verification capacity.

title: 90-Day Bridge Power for Robotaxi Depots
one_liner: Containerized battery-buffered charging stalls leased per stall per month so AV fleets can open depots years before the utility connects them.
customer: Robotaxi fleet operators and depot managers, autonomous-truck terminals, and electric delivery-van fleets that need charging capacity fast.
problem: Depot power is the scaling choke point. California lead times run about 6 months for a standard charging site, 1.9 years for a new circuit, 2.8 years for a substation upgrade and 8.9 years for a new substation, and depots compete with data centers for powered industrial land. Waymo alone has 3,871 vehicles and is aiming much higher.
solution: Modular systems combining second-life EV battery storage, a small grid tie (200-500 kW) and charging software that schedules vehicles around available energy. Sell 'stalls online in 90 days' as power-as-a-service. When the full grid connection arrives, the same assets convert to peak shaving and grid-services revenue.
why_now: Waymo, Tesla and Zoox (charging fares since August 10, 2026) are all scaling at once, and interconnection queues now outrun vehicle deployment. Data-center bridge power has proven that customers will pay a premium for time-to-power.
revenue_model: $600-1,000 per stall per month, or $0.30-0.45 per kWh delivered, on 3-5 year contracts, with asset financing behind them.
non_obvious_insight: For AV scale-up the binding constraint is interconnection time, not vehicles or software. Turning 'megawatts in two years' into 'kilowatts now, megawatts later' beats the utility's queue, and buffered assets keep earning after the grid arrives.
first_30_days: Get an LOI for a 20-stall pilot from one depot operator or delivery-van fleet. Source used battery modules through a reseller and integrate an existing containerized storage vendor's hardware rather than building your own. Target first revenue in month 4.

title: Leak-Proof Outsourcing Passport for Game Studios
one_liner: Contractor identity checks at first build access, per-recipient build watermarking and reusable vendor security attestations for the outsourcing chain (art, audio, QA, porting) that leaks unreleased games.
customer: Mid-size and AA/indie publishers that outsource to 20-200 external vendors. Also the vendors themselves (art studios in Poland, Vietnam, India and elsewhere, QA houses, localization and voice studios, freelance marketplaces) who need a portable credential to win work.
problem: Layoffs and cost-cutting push more production to external vendors and freelancers. Per the briefing, Ubisoft headcount fell from 18,666 to 16,590 and EA's $55B buyout, which closed 4 Aug 2026, aims to cut operating costs by putting AI throughout. Each vendor has weaker security than the publisher while unreleased builds are the crown jewels (GTA VI launches 19 Nov 2026, and past leaks like Rockstar 2022, Insomniac 2023 and Game Freak 2024 show the pattern). Remote contractors are also prime targets for identity fraud: North Korean IT-worker schemes hit 'nearly 70' and 'over 100' US companies in cases sentenced in Apr-May 2026, using deepfake-assisted interviews and stolen identities. Film has the MPA's Trusted Partner Network; games have no equivalent.
solution: A subscription 'passport' with five parts. (1) Contractor identity verification with liveness and injection-attack detection at onboarding and again at first privileged build access, tied to device posture. (2) A game-specific vendor security attestation, evidence-based (SSO, endpoint, repo hygiene) and shared across publishers so a vendor is assessed once. (3) Per-recipient forensic watermarking of builds, assets and design documents so a leak can be traced to a person or vendor. (4) Offboarding automation for contract end or layoff waves. (5) Insurer-ready evidence packages for cyber and E&O cover.
why_now: EA's leveraged buyout, Ubisoft's restructuring and Tencent-backed Vantage carve-out are all driving outsourcing. GTA VI's launch date will attract extortion attempts. North Korean IT-worker cases and deepfake interview kits make hiring-time identity checks insufficient. The IDScan.net breach (153M license scans) makes zero-retention verification a selling point (per briefing), and enterprise identity products are crowded but none focus on game supply chains.
revenue_model: Publishers pay $1.5-6k/month plus $30-80 per contractor-month. Vendors pay $200-500/month for a portable attestation badge, giving vendor-pays adoption. Watermarking priced per build distribution.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is not the publisher's own security but that each publisher re-audits the same few hundred vendors. A shared 'assess once, reuse everywhere' passport (film's TPN model) is cheaper for publishers and turns vendors into paying customers. Identity must be verified at the moment of privileged access rather than at hiring, because proxy interviews and deepfakes defeat interview-time checks.
first_30_days: Partner with 2-3 mid-size publishers or a co-dev/QA outsourcer. Draft a 40-question game-specific assessment, wire up an existing IDV API plus a device-posture check, and pilot with one outsourcing vendor. Offer a 'leak-trace drill' using watermarks on a demo build. Sell to publishers' security leads at $1.5k/month pilots.

title: Roll-Up of Compounding-Stranded Weight-Loss Clinics
one_liner: Buy distressed med spas and weight-loss clinics that lost their compounded GLP-1 margin, and convert them into aftercare-plus-aesthetics businesses.
customer: The clinics' patients, who pay memberships and procedures. Sellers are owners of weight-loss clinics, med spas and telehealth shells.
problem: FDA proposed excluding semaglutide, tirzepatide and liraglutide from the 503B bulks list on Apr 30, 2026 and sent ~55 warning letters to telehealth firms in Mar and Jun. Reportedly ~60% of med spas offered GLP-1 programs by 2025, many on compounded supply that peaked at ~30% of US volume. Owners want out, yet PE physician-practice deals are down ~50% in 2026, so buyers are scarce.
solution: Acquire 10-20 clinics at 0.3-0.8x revenue with seller notes and earn-outs. Convert to branded pill and vial cash programs, plus aftercare (muscle, nutrition, dose step-down), legal peptide offerings and aesthetics upsells. Centralize the medical director, billing and marketing.
why_now: The compounding cliff has stranded assets that are just patient relationships and licenses, while buyer capital retreated. 63% of 'Ozempic face' patients are cosmetic-clinic first-timers, so aesthetics cross-sell is real.
revenue_model: Clinic revenue of $199-399/month memberships plus procedures. Target ~25% EBITDA after integration, with a shared-services center.
non_obvious_insight: Distress plus absent buyers means near-free customer bases, and revenue per patient can rise after the switch to branded drugs plus aftercare. Earn-outs limit downside if patients churn.
first_30_days: Pull state med-spa and pharmacy lists and Instagram GLP-1 advertisers. Contact 100 owners, sign 2 LOIs with seller notes, and close the first acquisition of $150-300k with an integration playbook.
